facts.text: Boerum Hill takes its name from the Boerum family’s colonial farm that once covered most of the area during early Dutch settlement.
In 1973, the Boerum Hill Association’s long‑term advocacy led the Landmarks Preservation Commission to designate the neighborhood’s historic district.
More than 250 19th‑century row houses, many Greek Revival and Italianate, line Boerum Hill’s streets, reflecting its 1845‑1890 development.
Atlantic Avenue, a cultural corridor, hosts the long‑running Atlantic Antic festival and remains a hub for the neighborhood’s Arab‑American community.
The Pacific branch of Brooklyn Public Library, opened in 1905, is Brooklyn’s oldest Carnegie library and sits at 25 Fourth Avenue.
Spike Lee’s 1995 film Clockers, set in Boerum Hill, was filmed in the nearby Gowanus Houses, showcasing the area’s gritty streets.
